source.name: LaunchLoom owned design study
source.rightsEvidence: This is a LaunchLoom-owned original design study and its in-house rendered capture, stored for internal inspiration and implementation research.

heroGeometry.mode: urgent problem statement beside a high-visibility geometric signal
heroGeometry.alignment: left-anchored service type against an abstract warning frame
heroGeometry.viewport: one-screen problem summary with request and call actions

navigationGeometry.placement: light utility strip above the poster
navigationGeometry.mobile: short inline links and a visible phone action

typography.scale: oversized multi-line problem statement with tight supporting copy

palette.contrastIntent: high visibility with clean light-surface contrast

imageTreatment.crop: diagonal frame and circular diagnostic symbol
imageTreatment.focalPoint: graphic signal rather than decorative stock photography

motion.reducedMotion: keep the full geometry and issue index static

rules: reduce headline size before changing line breaks
place the signal shape after the opening copy
keep request and call actions visible and touch-safe

prohibitedPatterns: urgent claims unsupported by client facts

requiredSignatureElements.description: problem-led poster with a high-visibility geometric frame
high-contrast next-step band after the opening scene

acceptanceChecks: the visitor can identify the service and location intent quickly
the phone and request options are distinct
urgency is conveyed by hierarchy without fabricated availability claims
mobile preserves contrast and action visibility
referenceDna.annotatedDescription: Owned LaunchLoom urgent plumbing study. The full page pairs a deep-petrol problem poster and oversized diagonal yellow frame with an orange next-step band, a graphic diagnostic section, and a direct request close. The illustrated geometry is not live service status or a response-time promise.

review.scope: paired full-page evidence and transferable visual mechanics; not approval of sample business claims or production copy
